conditions: Real f continuous on [a,b], a<b; F continuous on [a,b] and differentiable on (a,b) with F'=f there.

evidence: Define G(x) as the integral of f from a to x. Continuity implies G'=f in the interior by the accumulation derivative theorem. Thus F-G has derivative zero and is constant by the mean-value theorem. Evaluate at a and b, using G(a)=0 and continuity at both endpoints.

conditions: f continuous on an interval containing a and x, with x interior.

evidence: For nonzero h, the difference quotient of the accumulation function is the oriented integral of f from x to x+h divided by h. Subtract f(x); the absolute error is bounded by the supremum of |f(t)-f(x)| on the segment. Continuity makes that bound tend to zero for either sign of h.
